I'll think through this as the farmer and then give my plan.

---

My 20 mu — most of it I run wheat-maize like always, and I keep 3 mu for chrysanthemum because the flowers sell for good money at the market and my wife and daughter-in-law help pick them. So wheat on 17 mu, maize on the same 17 mu after wheat harvest in June, and chrysanthemum on 3 mu.

For wheat, I plant in early October. I use the improved variety Jimai 22 — the seed dealer in town sells it and my neighbor old Wang got 520 kg/mu with it last year. For base fertilizer I put down about two bags of compound 15-15-15 per mu, that's 50 kg, before ploughing. Then at jointing in spring I top-dress with urea, about 15 kg/mu. So all together roughly 14 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K per mu. I plough once before sowing because rotary alone doesn't turn the straw in well enough. I irrigate from my well 3 times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray twice, once for aphids and once for wheat rust if I see it. I expect around 500 kg/mu, same as last year.

For maize I plant Zhengdan 958 right after wheat, no-tillage straight into the stubble — saves me diesel and time. I put 40 kg of compound 15-15-15 per mu at sowing plus 20 kg urea side-dressed at the big trumpet stage. So about 14 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat — I irrigate twice, once after sowing if no rain, once at tasseling. Spray once for corn borer. I get about 580 kg/mu usually.

For chrysanthemum I've been growing it maybe 8 years now. It needs more feeding than grain — I put down chicken manure compost plus compound fertilizer before planting, then top-dress with urea twice. Counting all the fertilizer, about 20 kg N, 12 kg P, 15 kg K per mu. Plough deep because roots go down. Irrigate 5 times, spray 4 times for aphids and leaf blight. Fresh flower yield around 800 kg/mu — that's where the real money is.

I spend more on chrysanthemum but the grain keeps the family fed and the flowers pay for everything else.
